newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No supply problems yet for Brazil coffee roasters.
newsitem.headline: No supply problems yet for Brazil coffee roasters.

text.p: There is currently sufficient supply of coffee in the internal Brazilian market, with roasters prepared to pay the higher prices being asked by producers, said the president of the Sao Paulo Coffee Industry Union.

A weekly indicator which gauges domestic supply has hovered between 4.18 and 4.73 since the beginning of the year and while this suggests selective availability, the indicator has not risen above five which would point to critical levels, said Nathan Herszkowicz.
This shows that "the coffee is arriving in the market and there is no problem getting hold of it," Herszkowicz said.

According to a survey of 12 companies in Sao Paulo, sales of roasted and ground coffee were 17.02 percent higher in January than in the same month last year and that over a 12-month period, the increase was 20.19 percent.

"The increase of sales, which should be celebrated, in reality represents a great problem as companies sold a great deal before they raised retail prices while at the same time they had to pay up to 80 reais more a bag (for green beans), " Herszkowicz said.
"The damages in the form of loss of cash flow and reduction in stocks perhaps has passed 30 million reais in Sao Paulo alone," he said.
The union expects however a fall in sales in February as a result of the rise in green bean prices.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
